newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico, U.S. officials sign 11 accords in meetings.
newsitem.headline: Mexico, U.S. officials sign 11 accords in meetings.

text.p: Mexican and U.S. cabinet members signed 11 accords on Monday, including a new agreement for cooperation in money laundering information, state news agency Notimex said.
The accords were reached as part of the annual U.S.-Mexico Binational Commission meetings between top officials from both countries.

The modification of an existing money-laundering agreement aimed at furthering shared information on banking operations suspected to be linked to drug trafficking. U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright and Mexican Foreign Affairs Minister Jose Angel Gurria signed the accord.

Also discussed in the high-level meetings were the expansion of the cross-border Matamoros-Brownsville bridge and a new bridge in the region. Funding for a new bridge from Ojinaga, Chihuahua state to Presidio in southern Texas.

The two governments pledged to work together against forest fires and other natural disasters, the news agency said. Two agreements were signed to protect the environment along the shared border, it added.
Another accord prohibited wild duck hunting in both countries from March 10 to Sept. 1.
Cabinet members also signed an agreement to cooperate in technical assistance for aviation.
A final version of the accords and talks will be available in June, the agency said.
